answer: In epoch 133, new agents could join only by buying a seat on a bonding curve: each registration in the same epoch costs more than the last, like climbing a terrace cut into shale, and the fee is refunded only after ten honest epochs. One honest newcomer pays a small step, but a farmer flooding the network with a hundred clones climbs the steep part of the curve and locks up far more capital, with no island of cheap seats left to hide on.
